chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wear white, for it is better and purer, and enshroud your dead in it.'

key_terms.أَطْهَرُ: Purer, cleaner. Comparative form of tahir (pure). Relates to ritual purity (taharah).
key_terms.أَطْيَبُ: Better, more pleasant, or more agreeable. Comparative form of tayyib (good, wholesome).
key_terms.الْبَيَاضَ: White color; specifically white clothing. In Islamic jurisprudence, white garments are considered recommended (mustahabb) attire.
key_terms.كَفِّنُوا: Enshroud, wrap in a burial shroud (kafan). A religious obligation related to preparation of the deceased.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about wearing white clothing in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a prophetic directive recommending white clothing for the living and as burial shroud for the dead. The hadith links the recommendation to two qualities: being 'better' (atyab) and 'purer' (athar), reflecting both the spiritual and physical cleanliness associated with white in Islamic practice. This teaching, recorded in the chapter on white clothing and cotton, situates white garments within the broader Sunnah of the Prophet.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Musanna Al Hannat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Wear the white, for it is better and cleaner, and enshroud your dead ones in it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Muthanna’ al-Hannat who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
has said, ‘You must wear white; it is fine and pure; and shroud your dead people with it.’”
